Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1242 AM CDT Sun Aug 09 2026

Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE SOUTHERN GREAT LAKES...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts will be possible Monday
afternoon and evening from northern Illinois eastward into western
Pennsylvania. Isolated severe gusts and hail will also be possible
from parts of the central and northern Plains into the Midwest.

...Southern Great Lakes...
At mid-levels, west-northwesterly flow will be in place on Monday
from the northern Plains into the Great Lakes. A subtle mid-level
shortwave trough and an associated jet streak will move through the
Great Lakes. To the south of the jet streak, a cold front is
forecast to advance southward into northern Illinois, northern
Indiana and northern Ohio by mid afternoon. Low-level convergence
along the front will be a focus for convective development. To the
south of the front, surface dewpoints in the 70s F will contribute
to moderate to strong destabilization by afternoon, with MLCAPE
likely peaking in the 2000 to 3500 J/kg range. Thunderstorms are
expected to develop near the front and move east-southeastward into
the stronger instability during the afternoon and evening.

Along the instability axis in the late afternoon from Lincoln,
Illinois to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, the ECMWF has 0-6 km shear
around 30 knots. This should support a mixed mode, with short
intense line segments and embedded rotating storms possible. The
primary threat will damaging wind gusts, with the maximum threat
located ahead of any cold pool that can organize. The severe threat
could persist into the early to mid evening, especially if MCS
development takes place, maintained by increasing low-level flow.

...Central and Northern Plains/Midwest...
West-northwesterly mid-level flow will be in place over the
north-central U.S. on Monday. A subtle shortwave trough is forecast
to move east-southeastward across the northern Plains. At the
surface, a cold front is forecast to advance southward across
western South Dakota during the day, with a dryline extending
southward into western Nebraska. To the east of the dryline, surface
dewpoints in the 60s and 70s F will contribute to moderate to strong
instability by afternoon. Isolated thunderstorms appear likely to
develop near the dryline during the mid to late afternoon.
Additional isolated storms are expected to develop further east
along the moist axis from eastern Nebraska into Iowa.

Forecast sounding along the moist axis in the late afternoon have
MLCAPE peaking in the 3000 to 4000 J/kg range with 0-6 km shear
around 30 knots. This environment, combined with steep low to
mid-level lapse rates, will support isolated potential for severe
wind gusts and hail.

..Broyles.. 08/09/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0224 AM CDT Sun Aug 09 2026

Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE OHIO VALLEY AND CENTRAL APPALACHIANS...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts will be possible on Tuesday
over parts of the Ohio Valley and central Appalachians. Isolated
severe gusts and hail will also be possible from parts of the
central and northern Plains into the Midwest.

...Ohio Valley/Central Appalachians....
At mid-levels, west-northwesterly flow will be in place on Tuesday
from the northern Plains to the central and northern Appalachians.
Along the southern edge of the stronger mid-level flow, a
west-northwest to east-southeast corridor of moderate to strong
instability is forecast to develop by afternoon. It appears that an
outflow boundary from the previous day's storms will be located from
approximately north-central Illinois east-southeastward into
southern Ohio. Low-level convergence along this boundary will be a
focus for convective initiation. In the afternoon, thunderstorms are
expected to develop near the boundary and move east-southeastward
into the stronger instability over the Ohio Valley. A cluster of
strong to severe storms is expected, and MCS development will be
possible across the region.

Instability is forecast to be similar to the previous day, with
MLCAPE peaking in the 2000 to 3500 J/kg range. According to the
ECMWF, deep-layer shear may be a bit stronger with 0-6 km shear in
the 30 to 40 knot range. This would support supercells and short
intense line segments capable of severe wind gusts. The wind-damage
threat would become maximized if a cold pool can develop during the
late afternoon and early evening. The current thinking is that the
ECMWF has a better handle on where the outflow boundary will be than
other solutions, and the Slight Risk area has been placed favoring
the ECMWF scenario.

...Central and Northern Plains/Midwest...
West-northwesterly mid-level flow will remain over the north-central
U.S. on Tuesday. At the surface, dewpoints in the 60s and 70s F from
South Dakota and Nebraska eastward into Iowa will contribute to
strong destabilization by afternoon. MLCAPE is forecast to peak
above 4000 J/kg along parts of the moist axis by late afternoon. In
spite of the instability, large-scale ascent is forecast to remain
relatively weak. Isolated to scattered storms could still develop
along zones of low-level convergence. The strong instability along
with moderate deep-layer shear should support an isolated severe
threat from mid afternoon to mid evening. Severe wind gusts and hail
will be the primary threats. Due to the weak forcing, there is some
uncertainty as to where the greatest convective coverage will be.

..Broyles.. 08/09/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0358 AM CDT Sun Aug 09 2026

Valid 121200Z - 171200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Wednesday/Day 4 to Friday/Day 6...
From Wednesday to Friday, a broad mid-level cyclonic flow pattern is
forecast to remain in place across the Great Lakes and the
Northeast, as a ridge moves eastward from the northern Rockies into
the upper Mississippi Valley. At the surface, a cold front is
forecast to become quasi-stationary from the central and northern
Plains into the mid Missouri and Ohio Valleys. Low-level convergence
near this front will be a focus for convective development each day.


On Wednesday, model forecasts suggest that scattered thunderstorms
will most likely develop Wednesday afternoon along an axis of
moderate instability from western Nebraska into southwestern South
Dakota. The storms will be supported by a mid-level shortwave trough
moving across the north-central U.S. Moderate deep-layer shear near
the instability axis should support a severe threat during the
afternoon and evening. The models also suggest that a convective
cluster will form within a very moist and unstable airmass in the
central Appalachians Wednesday afternoon, where a wind-damage threat
will be possible.

On Thursday, the most favored corridor for convective development is
forecast from eastern Nebraska into central Illinois. However, the
models suggest that scattered convective coverage could be
concentrated overnight as low-level flow increases across the
region. A severe threat could develop during the day but would
remain relatively isolated due to a lack of storm coverage. An
isolated severe threat could also develop across parts of the
central and northern High Plains during the afternoon. However,
storms there will also likely be isolated due to a shortwave ridge
aloft.

On Friday, thunderstorm swill also be possible from the central
Plains eastward into the Ohio Valley during the afternoon and
evening. However, the most favored locations are likely to be
determined by outflow boundaries associated with the previous day's
convection. For this reason, uncertainty is substantial on Friday.

...Saturday/Day 7 and Sunday/Day 8...
Over the weekend, a mid-level shortwave ridge is forecast to move
across the north-central U.S., as west-northwesterly flow remains in
the Northeast. An axis of instability is forecast from the central
Plains into the Ohio Valley, which will be a focus for thunderstorm
development. It appears that an isolated severe threat could develop
along and near the instability axis each afternoon and evening.
However, uncertainty is considerable concerning the details of any
potential scenario.

..Broyles.. 08/09/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1215 AM CDT Sun Aug 09 2026

Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE MIDWEST...AND PORTIONS OF THE DAKOTAS...

...SUMMARY...
Scattered damaging winds may occur today into this evening from
southern Minnesota and eastern Iowa eastward across parts of
northern Illinois, southern Wisconsin, southern Lower Michigan,
northwest Ohio, and northern Indiana. Damaging wind and hail is also
expected across portions of the Dakotas.

...IA/MN into the Midwest...

Convection is expected to be ongoing this morning across parts of
southern MN into eastern IA. This early day activity could pose a
risk for damaging gusts. This activity is likely to continue to
spread eastward across the Lake Michigan vicinity through the
afternoon on the nose a of modest low-level jet and along a surface
front oriented across southern WI and Lower MI. This activity could
intensify as is moves into a destabilizing airmass by midday. 

Additional development is possible within the moisture rich warm
sector across northern IL/IN along the southern flank of ongoing
convection and/or outflow. Strong to extreme instability is
forecast, while vertically veering wind profiles support 30+ kt
effective shear magnitudes. Low-level SRH also will be enhanced
along the surface boundary. While damaging winds are expected to be
the primary hazard with convection, some risk for hail and a tornado
or two also will exist through evening. Depending on the evolution
of morning convection, it is possible higher probabilities will be
needed in subsequent outlooks.

...Dakotas and western NE...

A surface front is expected to develop southward across the central
Plains, becoming oriented across northern KS by tonight. Low-level
warm advection atop the boundary, and surface winds becoming
south/southeasterly with time will maintain 60s dewpoints across the
region. Within this post-frontal upslope regime, moderate
northwesterly flow aloft will persist. A modest south/southwesterly
low-level jet is also forecast to develop during the evening hours.
Low-level convergence within the warm advection regime and
increasing low-level jet may be sufficient for isolated to scattered
thunderstorm development. Supercell wind profiles and steep
low-level lapse rates will support initial storms capable of large
hail and damaging winds. If sufficient clusters/outflow
consolidation can occur, upscale growth during the late evening into
overnight hours is possible, with an increasing risk for swaths of
severe/damaging gusts.

...Southern Appalachians...

Scattered thunderstorm development is expected over higher terrain
within a seasonally moist and unstable airmass. Steepening low-level
lapse rates and high PW values may support locally strong gusts with
wet microbursts through early evening.

...AZ...

Modest easterly mid/upper flow will persist across the region on the
southern periphery of an upper high over the Four Corners. Another
day of hot conditions will promote steep lapse rates and modest
destabilization. As convection develops over higher terrain and
spread westward, strong outflow gusts may occur.

..Leitman/Moore.. 08/09/2026
